question: Can public, item-level NMNH Division of Fishes records recover a row-level link between this 89-row GBIF cluster and the older Albatross collection-lot numbers?
decision: The official NMNH Fishes search returned one matching museum record for each of the 89 GBIF ARK identifiers. Current catalog number, collection day, source locality and waterbody fields match row-for-row. The museum records keep the same compound locality text: all 53 records dated 29 January 1909 say “Manila Bay; Pucot River (Near Mariveles)” while their waterbody is “North Pacific Ocean, Manila Bay”; all 36 records dated 30 January say “Mariveles Bay and Pucot River, Mariveles Wharf; Manila Bay” while their waterbody includes Mariveles Bay and Manila Bay. The API payloads do not expose Fowler lot numbers 7885, 7893 or 7894. Keep all rows historical research-only; no exclusive river assignment, current presence, app species, coordinates, geometry or image reuse is approved.

method.gbifInput: Filter the previously captured 319-row Bataan preserved-specimen screen for Pucot River in locality, verbatimLocality or waterBody; retain each GBIF record identifier, catalog number, scientific name, event date, locality and waterBody.
method.request: One POST per GBIF ARK: action=1, qtype=12 (query string), view=keyword:grid, start=0, limit=1, terms="ark <internal-id>". The internal ID follows the search UI transformation: remove the ark:/65665/ prefix and its ARK type digit, then remove hyphens. 125 ms spacing was used between requests.
method.access: The institution’s public Fishes search interface returned the results without sign-in, API key, or access-control bypass. This was not the Smithsonian Open Access API and is not asserted to be a stable bulk API.
method.matchedIdentity: Each returned admuu ARK and darcx catalog number was compared with the GBIF row; the collection date was normalized to YYYY-MM-DD for day-level comparison.

nameComparison.note: The remaining GBIF source string is genus-level “Gerres”; NMNH also returns “Gerres”. It is not counted as a species-level record.

byDate.sourcePlace: Mariveles Bay and Pucot River, Mariveles Wharf; Manila Bay
byDate.waterBody: North Pacific Ocean, Mariveles Bay; Manila Bay

returnedFieldWithLotLikeName.interpretation: Literal field and values only. Its relationship, if any, to Fowler’s older lot numbers was not established.

nmnhCrosscheck.note: The three NMNH event IDs and the acqln field do not themselves establish a crosswalk to Fowler lots or an exclusive collection waterbody.

entries.sourceLocality: Pucot River near Mariveles, Manila Bay

historicalLocalityCrosscheck.crosswalkLimit: None of these old lot numbers appeared in the 89 returned NMNH record payloads. Date and place phrase similarity does not establish an item-level lot mapping.

interpretation.jan29: Museum data confirm the same compound Pucot River/Manila Bay place for all 53 rows, but still give Manila Bay as the waterbody and provide no coordinates; do not project these as river-only occurrences.
interpretation.jan30: Museum data confirm the same compound Mariveles Bay/Pucot River/Mariveles Wharf/Manila Bay phrase for all 36 rows; they do not name Mariveles River as the exclusive waterbody. Do not relabel them as river-only records.
interpretation.geography: No river centerline, estuary boundary, shoreline or municipal-water geometry was derived.
interpretation.currentness: Historical preserved specimens do not establish contemporary presence, abundance, habitat limits, catchability, legality or safety.

limitations: NMNH catalog search results are individual historical collection records, not a current biodiversity inventory.
The endpoint is the interface backend used by the NMNH Fishes search; its stability as a public bulk service was not established.
No item-level NMNH catalog-data license or image reuse terms were verified. The GBIF dataset CC0 statement is not transferred to Smithsonian content or record-linked media by inference.
GBIF supplies no coordinates for these 89 rows, and the NMNH returned records supplied no coordinate fields in the reviewed result payloads.
The source returns 65 distinct GBIF scientific-name strings; one record is genus-level and must not count as a species.
The older Fowler lot numbers remain unlinked to the modern USNM catalog numbers; the returned acqln values are not treated as equivalent identifiers.
followUp: Keep all 89 rows research-only. Do not add species or assign a specific waterbody from this cluster.
Continue the Central Luzon work with a separate, source-backed waterbody and current or otherwise well-scoped fish evidence; do not wait on government correspondence for this held cluster.

sources.supports: The 89-row Bataan GBIF preserved-specimen cluster and its ARK identifiers, modern catalog numbers, dates, locality strings, broad Manila Bay waterBody labels, and absence of coordinates.
The handwritten archival manuscript records old Albatross lot 7885 at Pucot River on 29 January 1909, and lots 7893–7894 at Mariveles River on 30 January 1909.
Official NMNH Fishes search payloads for 89 item-level ARK lookups; confirms matching modern catalog/date/locality/waterbody metadata but exposes no match to the Fowler lot numbers.

rawSnapshot.queryMethod: One public search-interface POST per ARK; see method.request.
